title: Updated report of COVID-19 vaccine safety monitoring in Japan: booster doses for Omicron variants and vaccinations for infants and young children.
ehr_evidence: a potential limitations of the report may include underestimation of the numbers and incidence rates of adverse events by using the spontaneous reporting data.
summary: A national-level descriptive pharmacovigilance report of COVID-19 vaccine safety (booster doses for Omicron variants in people aged ≥12 years and vaccinations for infants/young children aged 6 months to 4 years) in Japan using spontaneous adverse event reporting data until 12 March 2023.
key_findings: Reporting rates of serious adverse events (myocarditis/pericarditis, anaphylaxis, and death) associated with bivalent Omicron vaccines were generally not higher than those for any booster doses.
The reporting rate of serious adverse events was low in children aged 6 months to 4 years.

Among 8,186,613 and 43,397,362 Pﬁzer doses for Omicron BA.1 and BA.4/BA.5, there were 97 and 527 individual case safety reports from healthcare professionals and 171 and 603 from the marketing authorisation holder, respectively.

There were 39 and 18 confirmed cases of myocarditis and pericarditis for any Pﬁzer booster doses; no confirmed cases of myocarditis/pericarditis for Moderna bivalent vaccines, with 24 and 13 confirmed cases for any Moderna booster doses.
No additional safety-related regulatory actions were issued by the Japanese government since the introduction of these vaccines until April 2023.
captured_features: number of doses administered by manufacturer, dose number, age, and sex
number of individual case safety reports from healthcare professionals and marketing authorization holders
confirmed cases of myocarditis and pericarditis
reporting proportions/rates by manufacturer, dose number, age, and sex
study_design: Descriptive pharmacovigilance report based on spontaneous adverse event reporting (passive surveillance)
data_source_type: Pharmacovigilance database (spontaneous adverse event reporting system, Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare)
population: People aged ≥12 years receiving COVID-19 booster doses for Omicron variants and infants/young children aged 6 months to 4 years in Japan, as of 12 March 2023
exposure_domain: COVID-19 vaccination (monovalent and bivalent Omicron BA.1 and BA.4/BA.5 booster vaccines; Pﬁzer BNT162b2 and Moderna mRNA-1273)
limitations: Underestimation of the numbers and incidence rates of adverse events due to reliance on spontaneous (passive) reporting data, with no reliable denominator-based incidence and potential underreporting and confounding.
Descriptive design without a comparison/unvaccinated group limits causal inference.
data_availability_statement: The data for this report are available to the public (Japanese language only) in the webpage of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan ( https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf /shingi/shingi-kousei_284075.html).
